subject: Cognitive Science
title: Are Concepts Universal?
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Are Concepts Universal?.

hook.text: Every culture has a concept for water. But not every culture has a concept for "privacy."

buildup.text: Some concepts seem universal—colors, body parts, basic emotions appear in every language.

discovery.text: Eleanor Rosch found that even isolated tribes in Papua New Guinea grouped focal colors alike.

twist.text: Yet the Pirahã people of the Amazon have no precise number words—not even for "one."

climax.text: Some categories are wired by biology; others are built entirely by culture and language.

punchline.text: Nature sets the palette. Culture paints.

quiz.question: What did Eleanor Rosch discover about color categories?
options: Even isolated tribes grouped focal colors similarly
No two cultures share color terms
